text:
sara: Heads-up — support ticket from Acme: observed p99 spike on /v1/generate after last deploy. Dash shows p99 ~1.8s for the past 30m, but when I look at the raw histogram panel the bins don't seem to line up with the rollup panel. Customer is seeing increased latency and costs. https://dash.redwood/so/abcd :/

anish: Which dashboard panel are you comparing? rollup panel uses precomputed quantiles from our rollup job, histogram panel is raw buckets from ingest. They can diverge if bucketization changed or if rollup window differs.

lee: Quick check — did anyone change the histogram bucket boundaries in the ingest pipeline? I remember a change to use finer buckets for small latencies last week. That would shift quantile calculations.

metrics-bot: alert: p99(/v1/generate) > 1.5s for 30m. query_id=Q-7781 samples=34 rollup_window=5m

anish: snafu hypothesis: rollup job (quantile-approx) uses reservoir sampling + sketch with eps=0.01; dashboard rollup panel shows sketch-derived quantiles, raw histogram panel reconstructs quantile by interpolating buckets. Different algorithms => different p99s.

sara: Ok — customer wants a clear answer. Can we (a) confirm whether bucket boundaries changed, (b) repro the difference with exact queries, (c) propose mitigation?

lee: repro steps I'm running now:
```
# raw histogram pull
SELECT bucket, count FROM http_latency_buckets WHERE route='/v1/generate' AND ts BETWEEN now()-10m AND now();
# rollup quantile check (sketch query)
SELECT approx_quantile(0.99, latency_sketch) FROM rollups WHERE route='/v1/generate' AND window=5m;
```
I already see a boundary shift: old buckets ended at 200ms, new buckets end at 300ms for the 10-300ms range. That will push mass into larger bins and inflate reconstructed quantiles.

metrics-bot: query results: raw_histogram total_samples=142 buckets=["0-10":12,"10-50":40,"50-100":50,"100-300":30,"300+":10] ; rollup_sketch p99=1.78s ; reconstructed_p99_from_buckets ~1.3s

anish: Interesting — reconstructed p99 is LOWER than sketch p99 here. That implies sketch captured a heavier tail (maybe some outliers) not reflected in aggregated bucket counts due to sampling drop. Check ingestion sampling/ingest-rate-limiter around 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC (deploy time).

sara: I pulled traces for a few high-latency requests — they show retries and long backend queuing for a subset of keys. Could be a backend flakiness that the sketch kept but buckets undercounted due to ingester throttling.

oncall-bot: deploy history: deploy id=deploy-20260312-0211 by @infra. Featureflag: quantitative-bucket-refactor enabled.

lee: That featureflag is the bucket change. So we have three moving parts: bucket boundary change, ingest sampling/throttling, and a real backend regression for some requests. Explains mismatch.

anish: Mitigations: 1) short-term: rollback bucket refactor in the rollup job or add a compatibility transform so reconstructed histogram panels use legacy boundaries; 2) mid-term: unify quantile semantics — make dashboards query the same sketch source or both panels show same underlying query; 3) customer-facing: open SR, offer canary rollback of specific deploy or route fallback to older model to reduce tail.

sara: For now I'll propose to support: canary rollback for Acme + switch their org to dedicated routing that avoids the new deploy. Also patch dashboard annotations to indicate which quantile algorithm is being shown.

lee: I'll open an internal ticket for the bucket-compat transform and add a short-term grafana override.

metrics-bot: ticket created: MET-4521 "bucket-compat shim for histogram rollups" assigned to @lee, priority: high

anish: Also we should add a short runbook note: when p95/p99 diverge between rollup vs histogram, check (1) bucket boundaries, (2) rollup window/sampling, (3) ingest throttling, (4) backend retries/traces.

sara: Perfect. I'll reply to the customer with the proposed mitigation and ETA. Thanks all :thumbsup:
